A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DeSOPE study. Their text, equations, nine figures, and three tables support reliable comparison. Both contain ten pages ending with references; neither supplied PDF includes an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset statistics, mesh-alignment results in Table 2, pose-estimation benchmarks in Table 3, and occlusion/manipulation analyses in Figure 9.

after.justification: v2 retains the original DeSOPE experiments and analyses, including alignment results, benchmark scores, and tests under occlusion and human manipulation.

M1.justification: The reported alignment component changes from SCFlow2 in v1's Section 4.1 and Figure 3 to SCFlow in v2's Section 3.1, explicitly distinguished from SCFlow2 in Section 4.2. The six-view matching, RANSAC/Umeyama registration, and pose-refinement framework remain. Whether this reflects reimplementation or correction of the earlier description is unstated.

E1.justification: Both retain 26 categories, 104 instances, five indoor environments, and static/manipulation scenarios across the same deformation levels. The pretraining data sources also remain unchanged. Added examples of manipulation actions elaborate existing coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 and Figure 9 retain SCFlow2, FoundationPose, and GenPose. The manual-initialization versus automatic-refinement comparison also remains. SCFlow is identified as an alignment component, without becoming an additional evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Section 3.2 changes the reported pose-initialization consistency threshold from 0.05 radians, approximately 2.86 degrees, to 5 degrees; the translation threshold remains 5 cm. Benchmark metrics and baseline training arrangements remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Both retain the alignment-refinement comparison, pose-refinement examples, occlusion analysis, and manipulation analysis under 20% occlusion. Figure 4 redisplays the same underlying images with added padding; it introduces no new case study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The descriptive dataset distributions in Figure 5 are unchanged.

E6.justification: All 42 numerical entries in Table 2 are divided by ten: overall refined errors of 5.38, 7.19, and 9.33 become 0.538, 0.719, and 0.933 cm. Because v1 specifies no units, this establishes revised numerical reporting without demonstrating improved accuracy. Table 3's 24 scores and Figure 9's curves are unchanged.

T1.justification: The ray-sampling and loss definitions remain, with no added proofs or substantive derivations. Equation (4) drops the explicit s(x) argument, while Equation (3) retains the SDF loss and its weight; the stated objective is unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same dataset contribution, novelty claim, scale, and central finding that pose-estimation performance deteriorates with increasing deformation.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 newly attributes GenPose's smaller degradation partly to retraining on DeSOPE, whereas v1 attributes it to category-level generalization alone. Conversely, v2 removes Section 3.2's explicit discussion of stereo-depth noise and systematic discrepancies between depth-derived point clouds and scanned meshes.

D1.justification: Table 2 newly specifies centimeter units and RANSAC outlier removal with a 3 cm threshold. Section 3.1 explicitly states that only SCFlow's correspondence predictions are used. The approximately 90K pretraining meshes and nine million image pairs were already disclosed in v1; hardware and dataset-access information remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to SCFlow and the ZED2i camera, and distinguishes SCFlow's alignment role from the evaluated SCFlow2 method. The broader related-work discussion and positioning of DeSOPE remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Pretraining details move from Section 4.1 to Section 3.1, and dataset composition/capture paragraphs move ahead of annotation details in Section 3.2. Alignment-result prose and several captions are rewritten, while the overall section structure and much of the text remain.

P2.justification: Figure 4 adds padding around the existing image panels. Captions for Figures 3–5 and Table 2 are revised or expanded, with accompanying page reflow. All nine figures and three tables remain, and the plotted data and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Explicit units and the 3 cm outlier threshold make Table 2 more interpretable, while acknowledging GenPose's retraining improves the explanation of its relative robustness. These provide a limited gain in reporting quality despite removal of the depth-noise/scan-mismatch discussion. The unexplained tenfold rescaling and unchanged benchmark evidence do not establish stronger empirical support.
